title: Back to the Future
about: A teenager accidentally travels back to 1955 and has to get his parents to fall in love.

    StartersFrench friesHand cut, fried twice. Ready at 88 miles an hourHow to make it500g potatoes1 L vegetable oil, for deep frying1/2 tsp fine saltCut the potatoes into chips, rinse in cold water and dry thoroughly with a clean tea towel.Heat the oil in a sturdy deep pan to 140°C and blanch the chips in batches for 5 minutes without browning.Drain and cool the chips for 15 minutes (this rest is part of the cook time).Raise the oil to 185°C and fry in batches until crisp, drain, season with salt and serve in paper boats.MainsCheeseburgerGriddled onions, pickles, mustardHow to make it600g beef mince1 onion1/2 tsp salt1/4 tsp black pepper80g American-style cheese4 burger buns60g dill pickles, sliced30g yellow mustardDivide the mince into four loose balls and slice the onion very thin.Heat a griddle until very hot. Put the beef balls on it, top with onion and press firmly into thin patties. Season with salt and pepper.Cook 3 minutes, flip and cook a further 2 to 3 minutes until the centre reaches 75°C. Lay the cheese on top to melt.Toast the buns and fill with the patties, pickles and mustard.Doc's breakfastEggs, bacon, toast. Great Scott, no robot armHow to make it8 rashers of bacon4 eggs8 slices of white bread40g butterLay the bacon in a cold frying pan and cook over medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until crisp. Lift out onto a plate.Fry the eggs in the bacon fat, spooning the fat over the yolks until the whites are set.Meanwhile toast the white bread and spread with the butter.Plate the eggs with the bacon and buttered toast.SweetsJoey's cakeHe didn't make parole. Eat it anywayHow to make it350g butter, softened200g caster sugar4 eggs2 tsp vanilla extract250g self-raising flour150ml milk300g icing sugar1 tube blue writing icingHeat the oven to 180°C and line a 20 x 30cm tin. Beat 200g of the butter with the caster sugar until pale.Beat in the eggs one at a time with the vanilla, then fold in the self-raising flour and 125ml of the milk.Spread into the tin and bake for 30 to 35 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Cool completely.Beat the remaining 150g butter with the icing sugar and the last 2 tbsp milk until fluffy and spread over the top.Pipe WELCOME HOME JOEY across the cake with the blue writing icing.DrinksMilk, chocolateCold, sweet, with a straw.How to make it4 tbsp cocoa4 tbsp caster sugar900ml full cream milk4 strawsWhisk the cocoa and caster sugar with 100ml hot water until smooth.Stir in the cold full cream milk and chill for an hour.Stir again and pour into four tall glasses with a straw each.Coffee, no sugarBlack, nothing added. No Pepsi FreeHow to make it60g medium-ground coffee1 L waterBrew the ground coffee with the water in a filter coffee machine or pour-over.Pour the coffee black into four mugs. No sugar.
